question: Which of the following rock systems in India is the main source of coal deposits?
explanation: The peninsula, during the Upper Carboniferous period experienced crustal movements, which led to the formation of basin-shaped depressions. These depressions had countless terrestrial plants and animals, which were buried to form coal deposits in India known as the Gondwana Rocks. These are sedimentary rocks and found mainly in the Damodar, Mahanadi and Godavari Valleys of the peninsula. Gondwana rocks contain nearly 98 percent of India's coal reserves. Gondwana coal is much younger (younger than Archean, Dharwad, Cudappah and older than ocean trap, tertiary and quaternary) than the Carboniferous coal and hence its carbon content is low.

explanation: The weathering of the Archaean rocks yielded the earliest sediments and formed the oldest sedimentary strata, the Dharwar system. question: When it is noon at IST meridian what would be local time at \(120^{\circ}\) East longitude?
explanation: The Longitudinal Difference between the Indian Standard Time and \(120^{\circ}\text{E}\) longitude is \(37^{\circ}30^{\prime}\) (\(120 - 82.30 = 37.5^{\circ}\)). Also the difference of \(1^{\circ}\) longitude is = 4 minutes. So, the difference is = \(37^{\circ}30^{\prime} \times 4 = 150\text{ min}\) (Almost 2 hours 30 minutes). Thus if it is noon at IST meridian, then the local time at \(120^{\circ}\text{E}\) longitude will be 12 + 2:30 = 2:30 pm (14:30 Pm).

question: Which was the Capital of Andhra Pradesh when it was made a separate State in the year 1953?

In response to this, the Telugu speaking people of Madras State started the agitation under the leadership of Potti Shri Ramulu. He died after fast unto death of 56 days which directly enhanced the agitation. As a result Jawaharlal Nehru made a declaration for the formation of a new separate state for Telugu speaking people. so Andhra Pradesh emerged as a new state, founded (on linguistic basis) on October 1, 1953 and Kurnool was made its capital. At present the capital of Andhra Pradesh is Hyderabad. Due to the formation of Telangana (in 2014) state from Andhra Pradesh, Hyderabad will be the capital of Andhra Pradesh only for ten years. The latitude of Aurangabad's location (\(19^{\circ}53^{\prime}47^{\prime\prime}\text{N}\)) is in between the latitudes of Vadodara (\(22^{\circ}30^{\prime}\text{N}\)) and Pune (\(18^{\circ}31^{\prime}\text{N}\)). Thus statement (2) is correct. The latitude of Bangalore is \(12^{\circ}97^{\prime}\text{N}\) and the latitude of Chennai is \(13^{\circ}04^{\prime}\text{N}\). question: The limit of the territorial water of India extends upto:
explanation: The United Nations Convention on Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) creates a regime of governance for maritime zones that fall under national jurisdiction namely the territorial water, contiguous zone, exclusive economic zone (EEZ) and continental shelf. A country's territorial waters extend 12 nautical miles from its coastal baseline, contiguous zone extends upto 24 nautical miles from the coastline, and its Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends up to 200 nautical miles. The limit of the territorial water of India extends up to 12 nautical miles from the coast, where India has absolute right to use this area.
